question.prompt: Johann has \(64\) fair coins. He flips all the coins. Any coin that lands on tails is tossed again. Coins that land on tails on the second toss are tossed a third time. What is the expected number of coins that are now heads?

solutions.explanation:
A coin stops being tossed as soon as it lands heads, so it finishes tails only if all three tosses are tails. Independent fair tosses give this probability as
\[
\frac12\cdot\frac12\cdot\frac12=\frac18.
\]
Thus each coin finishes heads with probability \(1-\frac18=\frac78\).

One coin contributes \(1\) to the final head count with probability \(7/8\), and \(0\) with probability \(1/8\). Its average contribution is therefore
\[
1\cdot\frac78+0\cdot\frac18=\frac78.
\]
The total head count is the sum of the contributions from all \(64\) coins. Averaging these totals adds the individual averages, because each outcome's total is already the sum of its individual contributions. Hence the expected number of heads is
\[
64\cdot\frac78=\boxed{56},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
solutions.title: Track one coin and add its average contribution
